news_drafts.headline: Forest of Dean treasury investments fall from £14.494m to £9.252m in six months to September 2026
news_drafts.lead:
Forest of Dean District Council's treasury investments fell by £5.242m in the six months to 30 September 2026, from £14.494m at 31 March 2026 to £9.252m, according to its mid-year treasury management report to the Audit Committee.

The report shows both short-term investments and cash were reduced over the period. It says investments "are lower than expected due to internal borrowing to fund the capital programme". Internal borrowing means using the council's own cash to pay for capital spending instead of taking a loan, which saves interest but uses up the cushion.

The council's forecast balance sheet resources, which the report gives as net investments, fall further to £11.606m by 31 March 2027. The report sets out the position as part of the council's mid-year treasury management update and its second-quarter prudential indicators, the limits and measures every council must publish to show its borrowing is affordable.
news_drafts.paper_title: Report F.802 FoDDC Treasury Management Mid Term 2026_27 and Qtr 2 TM PI's v.1

news_drafts.headline: Forest of Dean's budget strategy shows a £3.327m cumulative gap from 2027/28 to 2030/31
news_drafts.lead:
Forest of Dean District Council's budget strategy for 2027/28, before its Cabinet on 5 November, restates the council's medium term financial strategy, its multi-year budget forecast. The strategy shows a balanced budget for 2026/27, then annual funding gaps of £0.508m in 2027/28 and £0.686m in 2028/29. The gaps are £1.411m in 2029/30 and £0.722m in 2030/31, a cumulative £3.327m. The paper takes the February 2026 forecast as the starting point for 2027/28 and says the figures will be updated as detailed budgets, funding information and deliverable savings proposals are developed.

The council's Future Deficits Reserve stood at £874,957 on 1 April 2026. The paper says it "may provide short-term support, but it is not a permanent solution to the structural funding gap." Total reserves at that date were £13.4m, including a General Fund balance of £1.015m.

The paper also gives the February 2026 forecast as a cumulative gap of £4.616m over five years. It says the funding position may show a slight improvement, but that "there are a number of items that still need clarifying in order to confirm this." The paper's own figures in section 5.4 total £3.327m, and it does not reconcile that with the £4.616m. A review of balances and reserves will go to Cabinet and Council in December, alongside the 2027/28 budgets.

news_drafts.headline: Forest of Dean council improves forecast but faces £3.3m five-year funding gap
news_drafts.lead: Forest of Dean Council's medium-term financial strategy (MTFS), the council's financial plan for the next three to five years, shows a forecast funding gap of approximately £3.3 million over five years to 2030/31, an improvement from the £4.6 million gap identified previously. The council achieved a balanced budget for 2025/26, but the local government auditor's annual report notes the council will face a funding gap from 2027/28 onwards. The auditor says the council will need further savings, transformation activity and income generation to ensure long-term financial sustainability.

findings.paper_title: F.803 Annex A - Capital Programme 2025-26 , item 10.
findings.headline: Five Acres, the largest scheme, is revised down from £12,734,480 to £12,725,970
findings.detail: Five Acres (provision of leisure, education and business facilities) accounts for the largest share of the programme. Its revised budget is £8,510 lower than approved. Its Levelling Up grant funding line is £6,544,380 in both columns.
findings.matters: Five Acres is the largest single scheme in this programme, so a finance officer at another council or a lender would want to know whether its budget is moving, even by a small amount.
findings.figures: Approved £12,734,480; revised £12,725,970; Government Grant for Levelling Up £6,544,380 in both columns
findings.quote: Five Acres Provision of Leisure, Education & Business Facilities 12,734,480     12,725,970

findings.paper_title: F.803 Annex A - Capital Programme 2025-26 , item 10.
findings.headline: Borrowing in the 2026/27 capital programme is unchanged at £3,890,100 in both the approved and revised budgets
findings.detail: The External/Internal Borrowing line shows £3,890,100 in both columns. The revised programme therefore adds no borrowing requirement, and the increase is met from capital receipts.
findings.matters: A lender or finance director tracking a council's new borrowing from its capital programme sees here that the revision adds none, so the borrowing requirement from this programme is unchanged.

findings.paper_title: F.803 Annex A - Capital Programme 2025-26 , item 10.
findings.headline: Revised capital programme for 2026/27 is £19,650,070, up from £19,379,540 approved, with the increase carried by waste vehicles and funded from capital receipts
findings.detail: The Waste Vehicles scheme rises from £4,933,600 to £5,209,520. Capital Receipts in the financing table rise from £4,933,600 to £5,204,130. The net programme increase of £270,530 is the waste vehicle increase less small reductions and additions elsewhere.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council, or a lender, can see the specific scheme and funding source behind a £270,530 increase in a capital programme that otherwise sits close to its approved total.
findings.figures: Approved total £19,379,540; revised total £19,650,070; Waste Vehicles £4,933,600 to £5,209,520; Capital Receipts £4,933,600 to £5,204,130

findings.headline: Chief Finance Officer reports that all treasury management activity in the quarter complied with the Treasury Management Code and the approved Strategy.
findings.detail: The paper reports every investment limit as met, including strategic pooled funds at £6,000k against an £8,000k limit and borrowing at £0 against a £10,000k authorised limit. The security indicator shows an average credit rating of A+ against an A- target.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council can compare the compliance position and the indicator set against their own Treasury Management Strategy.
findings.figures: £6,000k strategic pooled funds against £8,000k limit; £0 borrowing against £10,000k authorised limit; A+ average credit rating against A- target; £43.737m liquidity against £10m target

findings.headline: Council has cash flow cover agreements with Newent Town Council and St Briavels Assembly Rooms, both entered into in 2025/26.
findings.detail: The paper says these agreements were approved in the Treasury Management Strategy. No amounts or terms are given in this report.
findings.matters: Councils that provide cash flow cover to linked third parties carry a credit exposure, and the paper's approach to it is a useful comparator.
